ui.h: AI incidents in education and among young people
ui.protect: Child protection: no child victim and no child perpetrator is named on this site. A young person is named only when their family made the name public in court or in mainstream media.
ui.k_school: Happened in a school or university
ui.s_year_h: Cases per year, by where they happened
ui.s_year_c: Each case is counted once, by the year it was first reported. Where it happened is kept separate from who was involved: a teenager harmed by a chatbot at home counts as a young person, not as a school incident.
ui.s_age_h: Age of the young people involved
ui.s_geo_c: Countries with the most case files. Counts reflect where incidents are reported and researched, so they understate countries with less media coverage in the languages we monitor.
ui.method: How cases are included: a verified case file appears here when a person under 25 was harmed or involved, or when it happened in a school, university or education service. Each case records separately whether a young person was involved, their age group and where it happened. Data:
ui.lede: Verified cases from around the world in which AI harmed students, children, teenagers or the people and institutions that teach them, with statistics, case studies, how schools and authorities responded, and the prevention measures and laws that governments, regulators and education bodies have put in place.
ui.cs_c: Selected cases, with what happened and how schools and authorities responded, as recorded in each case file.
ui.r_c: The response recorded in each of the {n} case files that happened in a school or university, from the sources cited in the case file.
ui.prev_c: Measures that ministries, regulators, exam bodies and international organisations have adopted or published, with what each one does, as stated in the document.
ui.laws_c: Laws in force that criminalise sexual deepfakes of minors or regulate AI used in education or by young people.
